newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden to send envoys to S.Africa in Palme probe.
newsitem.headline: Sweden to send envoys to S.Africa in Palme probe.

text.p: Sweden said on Wednesday it would send investigators to South Africa to follow up new leads into the 1986 murder of Prime Minister Olof Palme after fresh revelations from former death squad leader Eugene de Kock.

"Swedish investigators will go down to South Africa as soon as preparations are complete to look into statements in connection with the murder of Olof Palme," deputy state prosecutor Solveig Riberdahl told a news conference.
Riberdahl said it was not yet clear who would be going or how long preparations would take.

South African journalist Philip van Niekerk told Swedish television news on Tuesday that De Kock, head of a police hit-squad who has been convicted of six apartheid-era murders, had pointed the finger of blame at a 56-year-old Swede.
Van Niekerk said De Kock had made the allegation in an recent interview held in prison.
The Cyprus-based Swede, a former member of the Swedish intelligence services, told Swedish news programme Aktuellt he denied the allegations.

De Kock and two other agents of the apartheid regime, Dirk Coetzee and Craig Williamson, have all swapped charges in recent days as the South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission seeks to apportion blame for apartheid atrocities.
De Kock said in court last week that fellow agent Williamson had been involved in the Palme murder as part of an operation dubbed "Long Reach".

Williamson, who has acknowledged a role in three bombings of anti-apartheid activists in the 1980s, including the killing of African National Congress member Jeanette Schoon and her daughter, denied the charge.
Coetzee, de Kock's predecessor at the police murder unit, countered on Saturday by saying Palme was killed by a former Rhodesian special forces soldier who was a member of Long Reach.
The man named by Coetzee denied any involvement.
Palme, who was one of the bitterest enemies of the apartheid regime, was gunned down on a Stockholm street in February 1986.
